title: Every School Needs a Buddy Program
source_body:
I am a transfer student who moved to this school six months ago. Based on my experience, I strongly believe that every school should have a buddy program for new students.
When I first arrived, I didn't know where the music room was or how the lunch line worked. These things seem small, but for a new student, they can be very stressful. A buddy, a classmate chosen to help a new student, could solve these problems easily. For example, a buddy can show the new student around the school and explain the class rules.
More importantly, a buddy program helps new students feel less lonely. Making friends in a new place takes time, and many transfer students spend their first weeks alone. Having at least one person to eat lunch with can make a huge difference.
Some people may say that students will naturally make friends without any program. However, not everyone is outgoing. Shy students, in particular, need a little help to start a conversation.
A buddy program does not cost much, and it benefits both students. The new student gets support, and the buddy learns kindness and responsibility. I hope our school will start one soon.

variants.prestudy:
As a transfer student who moved to this school six months ago, I can say from personal experience that every school should have a buddy program for newcomers.
When I first arrived, I had no idea where the music room was, let alone how the lunch line worked. Although such details may seem trivial, they can be surprisingly stressful for someone unfamiliar with the school. A buddy, a classmate specifically chosen to help a new student, could resolve these problems with little effort. For instance, a buddy could show the newcomer around the school and explain the unwritten rules of each class.
More importantly, a buddy program helps new students feel less isolated. Building friendships in an unfamiliar environment inevitably takes time, which is why many transfer students spend their first few weeks alone. Having even a single person to eat lunch with can make an enormous difference.
Some people may argue that students will naturally make friends without any formal program. However, not everyone is outgoing by nature. Shy students, in particular, often need a little encouragement to start a conversation.
Not only is a buddy program inexpensive, but it also benefits both participants. While the new student receives much-needed support, the buddy develops kindness and a sense of responsibility. I sincerely hope that our school will introduce one in the near future.
